title.zh: 卷一百九十四 列傳第一百十九 卓行
title.raw: 卷一百九十四 列傳第一百十九 卓行 Volume 194 Biographies 119: Outstanding Conduct

sentences.zh: 元德秀

translations.literal: Yuan Dexiu
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Dexiu

sentences.zh: 元德秀，字紫芝，河南河南人。

translations.literal: Yuan Dexiu, styled Zizhi, was a native of Henan in Henan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Dexiu, whose style was Zizhi, came from Henan in Henan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 質厚少緣飾。

translations.literal: His substance was solid and he used little adornment.
translations.idiomatic: He was plain and solid in character, with little taste for ornament.

sentences.zh: 少孤，事母孝，舉進士，不忍去左右，自負母入京師。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he was filial toward his mother. When he passed the jinshi examination, he could not bear to leave her side and carried her on his back into the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he served his mother with deep filial devotion. After passing the jinshi examination, he could not bear to leave her and carried her on his back all the way to the capital.

sentences.zh: 既擢第，母亡，廬墓側，食不鹽酪，藉無茵席。

translations.literal: After he was selected, his mother died. He built a hut beside her tomb, ate no salt or dairy, and slept on straw without a mat.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had passed the examination, his mother died. He lived in a hut beside her grave, ate no salt or dairy, and slept on straw without even a mat.

sentences.zh: 服除，以窶困調南和尉，有惠政。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was assigned as magistrate of Nanhe on account of his poverty, and he had a benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended, poverty led to his appointment as magistrate of Nanhe, where his benevolent rule won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 黜陟使以聞，擢補龍武軍錄事參軍。

translations.literal: The touring inspector reported this, and he was promoted to Recorder of the Longwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: The touring inspector reported his conduct to the throne, and he was promoted to recorder of the Longwu Army.

sentences.zh: 德秀不及親在而娶，不肯婚，人以為不可絕嗣，答曰：「兄有子，先人得祀，吾何娶為？

translations.literal: Dexiu had not married while his parents were alive, and he refused to wed. People said he must not cut off his line, but he replied: "My elder brother has a son; our forebears will receive sacrifice—why should I marry?"
translations.idiomatic: Dexiu had never married while his parents lived, and he now refused to wed at all. People urged that he must not let the line die out, but he answered: "My elder brother has a son; our ancestors will still receive offerings—why should I take a wife?"

sentences.zh: 」初，兄子繈褓喪親，無資得乳媼，德秀自乳之，數日湩流，能食乃止。

translations.literal: Earlier, his brother's infant son had lost both parents and there was no means to hire a wet nurse; Dexiu suckled the child himself until milk flowed; only when it could eat did he stop.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, his brother's infant son had lost both parents and the family could not afford a wet nurse, so Dexiu nursed the child himself until milk came; only when the boy could eat solid food did he stop.

sentences.zh: 既長，將為娶，家苦貧，乃求為魯山令。

translations.literal: When the boy grew up and a match was to be arranged, the family was desperately poor, so he sought appointment as magistrate of Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: When the boy grew up and a marriage had to be arranged, the household was desperately poor, so Dexiu sought appointment as magistrate of Lushan.

sentences.zh: 前此墮車足傷，不能趨拜，太守待以客禮。

translations.literal: Before this he had fallen from a cart and injured his foot, so he could not bow in haste; the prefect treated him with the honors due a guest.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier fallen from a cart and injured his foot, so he could not perform the quick bow; the prefect therefore received him with the courtesy due a guest.

sentences.zh: 有盜系獄，會虎為暴，盜請格虎自贖，許之。

translations.literal: A thief was held in prison. Tigers were ravaging the region, and the thief asked to fight the tiger to redeem himself; Dexiu agreed.
translations.idiomatic: A thief was in custody when tigers began ravaging the district; the man asked to slay a tiger in exchange for his freedom, and Dexiu consented.

sentences.zh: 吏白：「彼詭計，且亡去，無乃為累乎？

translations.literal: An officer reported: "That is a trick, and he will soon flee—will this not bring trouble upon us?"
translations.idiomatic: An officer warned him: "That is only a ruse—he will run off, and we shall be blamed for it."

sentences.zh: 」德秀曰：「許之矣，不可負約。

translations.literal: Dexiu said: "It has been promised; the agreement cannot be broken."
translations.idiomatic: Dexiu replied: "I have already promised him; I cannot break my word."

sentences.zh: 即有累，吾當坐，不及餘人。

translations.literal: "If there is trouble, I alone shall bear punishment; it shall not extend to others."
translations.idiomatic: "If blame falls, I alone shall answer for it—not the rest of you."

sentences.zh: 」明日，盜屍虎還，舉縣嗟嘆。

translations.literal: The next day the thief returned with the tiger's carcass, and the whole county sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the thief returned with the tiger's body, and the whole county marveled.

sentences.zh: 玄宗在東都，酺五鳳樓下，命三百里縣令、刺史各以聲樂集。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong was in the eastern capital, he held a feast beneath the Hall of Five Phoenixes and ordered magistrates and prefects from three hundred li around to gather with music.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Xuanzong was at the eastern capital, he held a grand feast beneath the Hall of Five Phoenixes and summoned magistrates and prefects from three hundred li around, each to present his district's music.

sentences.zh: 是時頗言帝且第勝負，加賞黜。

translations.literal: At the time many said the emperor would rank their performances and bestow rewards or dismissals accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor had it that the emperor would rank the performances and reward or dismiss officials accordingly.

sentences.zh: 河內太守輦優伎數百，被錦繡，或作犀象，瑰譎光麗。

translations.literal: The Prefect of Henei brought several hundred entertainers in brocade, some costumed as rhinoceroses and elephants, bizarre and dazzlingly bright.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Henei paraded several hundred performers clad in brocade, some dressed as rhinoceroses and elephants, all bizarre and dazzling.

sentences.zh: 德秀惟樂工數十人，聯袂歌《於蒍於》。

translations.literal: Dexiu had only several dozen musicians, who sang arm in arm "Yu xian yu."
translations.idiomatic: Dexiu brought only a few dozen musicians, who sang arm in arm his song "Yu xian yu."

sentences.zh: 《於蒍於》者，德秀所為歌也。

translations.literal: "Yu xian yu" was a song Dexiu himself had composed.
translations.idiomatic: "Yu xian yu" was a song of his own composition.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，異之，嘆曰：「賢人之言哉！

translations.literal: The emperor heard this, marvelled, and exclaimed: "The words of a worthy man!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard it, marveled, and cried: "These are the words of a worthy man!"

sentences.zh: 」謂宰相曰：「河內人其塗炭乎？

translations.literal: He said to the chief ministers: "Are the people of Henei being crushed to charcoal?"
translations.idiomatic: He said to his chief ministers: "Are the people of Henei being ground to ashes?"

sentences.zh: 」乃黜太守，德秀益知名。

translations.literal: He then dismissed the prefect, and Dexiu became still more renowned.
translations.idiomatic: He dismissed the prefect, and Dexiu's fame spread still further.

sentences.zh: 所得奉祿，悉衣食人之孤遺者。

translations.literal: Whatever salary he received he used entirely to clothe and feed orphans and the bereft.
translations.idiomatic: Every penny of his salary went to clothe and feed orphans and the destitute.

sentences.zh: 歲滿，笥余一縑，駕柴車去。

translations.literal: When his term ended, only one piece of silk remained in his chest; he drove off in a firewood cart.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended, only one bolt of silk remained in his box; he left in a firewood cart.

sentences.zh: 愛陸渾佳山水，乃定居。

translations.literal: He loved the fine mountains and waters of Luhun and settled there permanently.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the fine landscape of Luhun and made his home there.

sentences.zh: 不為墻垣扃鑰，家無仆妾。

translations.literal: He built no walls or bolts; his household had no servants or concubines.
translations.idiomatic: He put up no walls or locks, and kept neither servants nor concubines.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，日或不爨。

translations.literal: In years of famine he sometimes went a day without cooking.
translations.idiomatic: In famine years he sometimes went whole days without lighting a fire.

sentences.zh: 嗜酒，陶然彈琴以自娛。

translations.literal: He loved wine and would play the zither in serene pleasure to amuse himself.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine and would play the zither in tranquil delight to amuse himself.

sentences.zh: 人以酒肴從之，不問賢鄙為酣飫。

translations.literal: When people brought him food and drink, he made no distinction between the worthy and the base, but feasted with all until satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever brought him food and drink, worthy or base, he would feast with them until all were satisfied.

sentences.zh: 是時程休、邢宇、宇弟宙、張茂之、李、族子丹叔、惟嶽、喬潭、楊拯、房垂、柳識皆號門弟子。

translations.literal: At this time Cheng Xiu, Xing Yu, Yu's younger brother Zhou, Zhang Mao-zhi, Li, his clansmen Dan-shu and Wei-yue, Qiao Tan, Yang Zheng, Fang Chui, and Liu Shi were all called his disciples at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Cheng Xiu, Xing Yu, Yu's younger brother Zhou, Zhang Mao-zhi, Li Shi, his clansmen Dan-shu and Wei-yue, Qiao Tan, Yang Zheng, Fang Chui, and Liu Shi were all known as his disciples.

sentences.zh: 德秀善文辭，作《蹇士賦》以自況。

translations.literal: Dexiu was skilled in literary expression and wrote "The Lame Gentleman Fu" to portray his own situation.
translations.idiomatic: Dexiu excelled at letters and wrote "The Lame Gentleman Fu" to portray himself.

sentences.zh: 房琯每見德秀，嘆息曰：「見紫芝眉宇，使人名利之心都盡。

translations.literal: Whenever Fang Guan saw Dexiu, he would sigh: "To behold Zizhi's brow alone makes every thought of fame and profit vanish."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Fang Guan met Dexiu he would sigh and say: "A glimpse of Zizhi's countenance makes every craving for fame and gain disappear."

sentences.zh: 」蘇源明常語人曰：「吾不幸生衰俗，所不恥者，識元紫芝也。」

translations.literal: Su Yuanming often said to others: "Unhappy am I to have been born in a declining age—the one thing I am not ashamed of is having known Yuan Zizhi."
translations.idiomatic: Su Yuanming often told others: "Unhappy am I to have been born in a decadent age; the one thing I am not ashamed of is having known Yuan Zizhi."

sentences.zh: 天寶十三載卒，家惟枕履簞瓢而已。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianbao he died, and his household possessed nothing but pillows, shoes, baskets, and gourds.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirteenth year of Tianbao, leaving his household with nothing but pillows, shoes, baskets, and gourds.

sentences.zh: 潭時為陸渾尉，庀其葬。

translations.literal: Tan, who was then magistrate of Luhun, arranged his burial.
translations.idiomatic: Tan, then magistrate of Luhun, arranged his funeral.

sentences.zh: 族弟結哭之慟，或曰：「子哭過哀，禮歟？

translations.literal: His younger clansman Jie mourned with extreme grief. Someone said: "Your weeping exceeds propriety—is this ritual?"
translations.idiomatic: His younger clansman Yuan Jie mourned him with piercing grief. Someone said: "Your grief exceeds propriety—is this in accord with ritual?"

sentences.zh: 」結曰：「若知禮之過，而不知情之至。

translations.literal: Jie said: "If you know that ritual can be excessive, you do not yet know how far feeling can go."
translations.idiomatic: Jie replied: "If you know that ritual can be excessive, you do not yet know how deep feeling can run."

sentences.zh: 大夫弱無固，性無專，老無在，死無余，人情所耽溺、喜愛、可惡者，大夫無之。

translations.literal: Our Great Man had no weakness of will in youth, no obstinacy of nature, no dependence in old age, and no surplus at death. All that human feeling drowns in, loves, or detests—he had none of it.
translations.idiomatic: The Master had no weakness of will in youth, no stubbornness of temperament, no clinging in old age, and no surplus at death. Whatever human feeling drowns in, loves, or hates—he had none of it.

sentences.zh: 生六十年未嘗識女色、視錦繡，未嘗求足，而茍辭、佚色，未嘗有十畝之地、十尺之舍、十歲之僮，未嘗完布帛而衣，具五味之餐。

translations.literal: Sixty years he lived without ever knowing the sight of women, without ever looking on brocade, without ever seeking more than enough; yet he would readily decline fine words and alluring forms. He never had ten mu of land, ten chi of dwelling, or ten years' service from a boy; he never wore whole cloth, and he never took a meal with all five flavors.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty years he lived without ever knowing women, without ever looking on brocade, without ever seeking more than enough—yet he would readily turn aside fine words and alluring faces. He never owned ten mu of land, ten feet of dwelling, or a boy of ten years' service; he never wore whole cloth, and never ate a meal with all five flavors.

sentences.zh: 吾哀之，以戒荒淫貪佞、綺紈粱肉之徒耳。」

translations.literal: "I mourn him to warn those given to dissipation, greed, flattery, brocade silks, and rich meat."
translations.idiomatic: "I mourn him to warn those given to dissipation, greed, flattery, brocade silks, and rich meat."

sentences.zh: 李華兄事德秀，而友蕭穎士、劉迅。

translations.literal: Li Hua treated Dexiu as an elder brother, and was friends with Xiao Yingshi and Liu Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hua honored Dexiu as an elder brother and befriended Xiao Yingshi and Liu Xun.

sentences.zh: 及卒，華謚曰文行先生。

translations.literal: When Dexiu died, Hua gave him the posthumous title Master of Literary Conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, Hua gave him the posthumous title Master of Literary Conduct.

sentences.zh: 天下高其行，不名，謂之元魯山。

translations.literal: The empire revered his conduct and would not speak his personal name, calling him instead Yuan of Mount Lu.
translations.idiomatic: The empire revered his conduct and would not speak his personal name, calling him Yuan of Mount Lu instead.

sentences.zh: 華於是作《三賢論》。

translations.literal: Hua thereupon wrote "An Essay on Three Worthies."
translations.idiomatic: Hua thereupon wrote "An Essay on Three Worthies."

sentences.zh: 或問所長，華曰：「德秀誌當以道紀天下，迅當以《六經》諧人心，穎士當以中古易今世。

translations.literal: When asked wherein each excelled, Hua said: "Dexiu's intent was to order the empire by the Way; Xun's was to harmonize men's hearts with the Six Classics; Yingshi's was to replace the present age with the middle antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: When asked what each excelled at, Hua said: "Dexiu aimed to order the empire by the Way; Xun aimed to harmonize men's hearts with the Six Classics; Yingshi aimed to replace the present age with the middle antiquity."

sentences.zh: 德秀欲齊愚智，迅感一物不得其正，穎士呼吸折節而獲重祿，不易一刻之安易，於孔子之門，皆達者歟！

translations.literal: Dexiu wished to make the foolish and the wise equal; Xun was moved whenever a single thing failed to attain its proper place; Yingshi would bend and bow for breath to obtain heavy emoluments, unwilling to trade one moment's ease—yet within Confucius's gate, are these all adept men?"
translations.idiomatic: Dexiu wished to level the foolish and the wise; Xun was stirred whenever a single thing fell short of its proper place; Yingshi would bend and bow with every breath to win heavy rewards, unwilling to trade a moment's ease—yet are all of these adept men within Confucius's gate?"

sentences.zh: 使德秀據師保之位，瞻形容，乃見其仁。

translations.literal: Let Dexiu occupy the position of tutor and protector, and gaze on his countenance—then you see his humanity.
translations.idiomatic: Place Dexiu in the post of tutor and protector and look upon his face—then you see his humanity.

sentences.zh: 迅被卿佐服，居賓友，謀治亂根源，參乎元精，乃見其妙。

translations.literal: Let Xun wear the garb of a chief minister's aide and dwell among guests and friends, deliberating the roots of order and chaos and communing with the primordial essence—then you see his subtlety.
translations.idiomatic: Let Xun wear the robes of a chief minister's aide, dwell among guests and friends, and deliberate the roots of order and chaos while communing with the primordial essence—then you see his subtlety.

sentences.zh: 穎士若百煉之剛，不可屈，使當廢興去就、一生一死間，而後見其節。

translations.literal: Let Yingshi be steel refined a hundred times, impossible to bend; let him face the going and staying of dynasties, the single span between life and death—then you see his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Let Yingshi be steel tempered a hundred times, impossible to bend; set him at the turning point between a dynasty's rise and fall, between life and death—then you see his integrity.

sentences.zh: 德秀以為王者作樂崇德，天人之極致，而辭章不稱，是無樂也，於是作《破陣樂辭》以訂商、周。

translations.literal: Dexiu held that when kings made music to exalt virtue, that was the utmost of Heaven and man, yet unworthy wording made it as if there were no music; he therefore composed lyrics for "Breaking the Battle Array" to correct the Shang and Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dexiu held that when kings made music to exalt virtue, that was the utmost of Heaven and man, yet unworthy words made it as though there were no music at all; he therefore composed lyrics for "Breaking the Battle Array" to correct the music of Shang and Zhou.

sentences.zh: 迅世史官，述《禮》、《易》、《書》、《春秋》、《詩》為《古五說》，條貫源流，備古今之變。

translations.literal: Xun, being a historian of the age, set forth the Ritual, Changes, Documents, Annals, and Odes in "The Ancient Five Expositions," threading origins and developments and encompassing change ancient and modern.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, a historian of his age, set forth the Ritual, Changes, Documents, Annals, and Odes in "The Ancient Five Expositions," threading origins and developments and encompassing change from antiquity to the present.

sentences.zh: 穎士尤罪子長不編年而為列傳，後世因之，非典訓也。

translations.literal: Yingshi especially faulted Master Zi-chang for not compiling annals but writing biographical accounts, which later generations followed—this was not canonical instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Yingshi especially faulted Master Zichang for arranging annals by year but writing biographical accounts instead, which later generations followed—this was not canonical teaching.

sentences.zh: 自《春秋》三家後，非訓齊生人不錄。

translations.literal: After the three schools of the Spring and Autumn, only those who received the instruction of Qi were recorded.
translations.idiomatic: After the three schools of the Spring and Autumn, he recorded only those who had received instruction in Qi.

sentences.zh: 然各有病，元病酒，劉病賞物，蕭病貶惡太亟、獎能太重。

translations.literal: Yet each had a flaw: Yuan's flaw was wine; Liu's was cherishing possessions; Xiao's was condemning evil too urgently and praising talent too heavily.
translations.idiomatic: Yet each had a flaw: Yuan's was wine; Liu's was cherishing possessions; Xiao's was condemning evil too harshly and praising talent too lavishly.

sentences.zh: 若取其節，皆可為人師也。

translations.literal: If you take their integrity, each could serve others as a teacher.
translations.idiomatic: If you take their integrity alone, each could serve as another's teacher.

sentences.zh: 」世謂篤論。

translations.literal: The age called this sincere judgment.
translations.idiomatic: His contemporaries called this a sincere and weighty judgment.

sentences.zh: 休，字士美，廣平人。

translations.literal: Xiu, styled Shimei, was a man of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xiu, styled Shimei, was from Guangping.

sentences.zh: 宇字紹宗，宙字次宗，河間人。

translations.literal: Yu, styled Shaozong; Zhou, styled Cizong—men of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Yu, styled Shaozong, and his younger brother Zhou, styled Cizong, were from Hejian.

sentences.zh: 茂之，字季豐，南陽人。

translations.literal: Mao-zhi, styled Jifeng, was a man of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao-zhi, styled Jifeng, was from Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 字伯高，丹叔字南誠，惟嶽字謨道，趙人。

translations.literal: [Li], styled Bogao; Dan-shu styled Nancheng; Wei-yue styled Modao—men of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi, styled Bogao; his clansmen Dan-shu, styled Nancheng, and Wei-yue, styled Modao, were from Zhao.

sentences.zh: 潭字源，梁人。

translations.literal: Tan, styled Yuan, was a man of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Tan, styled Yuan, was from Liang.

sentences.zh: 垂，字翼明，清河人。

translations.literal: Chui, styled Yiming, was a man of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Chui, styled Yiming, was from Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 拯，字齊物，隋觀王雄後，舉進士，終右驍衛騎曹參軍。

translations.literal: Zheng, styled Qiwu, a descendant of Sui's Prince of Guan Xiong, passed the jinshi examination, and ended as Cavalry Retainer of the Right Martial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zheng, styled Qiwu, a descendant of Sui's Prince of Guan Xiong, passed the jinshi examination and ended his career as cavalry retainer of the Right Martial Guards.

sentences.zh: 擢制科，遷南華令。

translations.literal: Selected in the special examination, he was transferred to be magistrate of Nanhua.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shi passed the special examination and was appointed magistrate of Nanhua.

sentences.zh: 大水，他縣饑，人至相屬，為具{衍食}鬻，及去，糗糧送之，吏為立碑。

translations.literal: Great flood; other counties were stricken with famine and people came in succession; he provided thin gruel for sale, and when they left he sent them with dry provisions; the clerks erected a stele for him.
translations.idiomatic: When great floods struck and neighboring counties starved, refugees came in an unbroken stream; he prepared thin gruel for them to buy, and when they departed he sent them off with dry provisions; the clerks erected a stele in his honor.

sentences.zh: 安祿山亂，客清河，為乞師平原太守顏真卿，一郡獲全。

translations.literal: During An Lushan's rebellion he sojourned in Qinghe, pleaded for troops from Yan Zhenqing, prefect of Pingyuan, and one whole commandery was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: During An Lushan's rebellion he stayed in Qinghe and begged Yan Zhenqing, prefect of Pingyuan, for troops, thereby preserving an entire commandery.

sentences.zh: 歷廬州刺史。

translations.literal: He served successively as prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as prefect of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 拯與名最著，潭、識以文傳後。

translations.literal: Zheng and Ming were most renowned; Tan and Shi passed their fame down through literature.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng and Chui were most renowned; Tan and Shi handed their fame down through literature.

sentences.zh: 權臯，字士繇，秦州略陽人，徙潤州丹徒，晉安丘公翼十二世孫。

translations.literal: Quan Gao, styled Shiyao, was a native of Lueyang in Qinzhou, moved to Dantu in Runzhou, and was the twelfth-generation descendant of Duke Anqiu Yi of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Gao, styled Shiyao, was born in Lueyang, Qinzhou, and later moved to Dantu in Runzhou; he was the twelfth-generation descendant of Duke Anqiu Yi of the Jin dynasty.

sentences.zh: 父倕與席豫、蘇源明以藝文相友，終羽林軍參軍。

translations.literal: His father Kun, together with Xi Yu and Su Yuanming, befriended one another through literary arts, and ended as Retainer of the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kun befriended Xi Yu and Su Yuanming through their shared love of letters and ended his career as retainer of the Feathered Forest.

sentences.zh: 臯擢進士第，為臨清尉，安祿山籍其名，表為薊尉，署幕府。

translations.literal: Gao passed the jinshi and served as magistrate of Linqing; An Lushan registered his name and summoned him as magistrate of Ji, appointing him to his secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Gao passed the jinshi examination and served as magistrate of Linqing; An Lushan registered his name, appointed him magistrate of Ji, and assigned him to his secretariat.

sentences.zh: 臯度祿山且叛，以其猜虐不可諫，欲行，慮禍及親。

translations.literal: Gao judged that Lushan would soon rebel and that his suspicious cruelty could not be remonstrated with; he wished to leave but feared harm would reach his kin.
translations.idiomatic: Gao saw that Lushan would soon rebel and that his suspicious cruelty made remonstrance useless; he wished to flee but feared his family would suffer for it.

sentences.zh: 天寶十四載，使獻俘京師，還過福昌尉仲謨。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Tianbao he was sent to present captives in the capital; returning, he passed Magistrate Zhongmo of Fuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Tianbao he was sent to present captives in the capital; on his return he passed through Fuchang, where the magistrate was Zhongmo.

sentences.zh: 謨妻，臯妹也，密約以疾召之，謨來，臯陽喑，直視謨而瞑。

translations.literal: Zhongmo's wife was Gao's younger sister; they made a secret pact to summon him on pretext of illness. When Zhongmo came, Gao feigned muteness, stared straight at Zhongmo, and closed his eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongmo's wife was Gao's younger sister; they secretly agreed to summon him on pretext of illness. When Zhongmo arrived, Gao feigned muteness, stared directly at him, and closed his eyes.

sentences.zh: 謨為盡哀，自含斂之。

translations.literal: Zhongmo mourned him with full grief and personally performed the encoffining.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongmo mourned him with full ritual grief and personally performed the encoffining.

sentences.zh: 臯逸去，人無知者。

translations.literal: Gao slipped away; no one knew.
translations.idiomatic: Gao slipped away unnoticed.

sentences.zh: 吏以詔書還臯母，母謂實死，慟哭感行路，故祿山不之虞，歸其母。

translations.literal: The clerks returned the imperial edict to Gao's mother; she believed he had truly died and wept so movingly that passersby were stirred; thus Lushan suspected nothing and returned his mother.
translations.idiomatic: The clerks returned the imperial edict to Gao's mother; believing he had truly died, she wept so bitterly that passersby were moved to tears; Lushan therefore suspected nothing and sent his mother home.

sentences.zh: 臯潛候於淇門，奉侍晝夜南奔，客臨淮，為驛亭保以诇北方。

translations.literal: Gao lay in wait at Qi Gate, attending her day and night as they fled south, stopping at Huaiyin and having the relay station secured to reconnoiter the north.
translations.idiomatic: Gao lay in wait at Qi Gate, attending his mother day and night as they fled south; they stopped at Huaiyin, where he secured the relay station to spy on movements in the north.

sentences.zh: 既度江而祿山反，天下聞其名，爭取以為屬。

translations.literal: Once they had crossed the Yangzi, Lushan rebelled; all under heaven heard his name and contended to claim him as their subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: Once they had crossed the Yangzi, Lushan rebelled; all under heaven heard Gao's name and vied to claim him as their man.

sentences.zh: 高適表試大理評事、淮南采訪判官。

translations.literal: Gao Shi memorialized to try him as Judge of the Grand Court and as Investigation Commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shi recommended him for trial appointment as judge of the Grand Court and as investigation commissioner of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 永王舉兵，脅士大夫，臯詭姓名以免。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yong raised troops and coerced the scholar-officials, Gao falsified his name to escape.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yong raised troops and coerced scholar-officials into his service, Gao concealed his identity under a false name to escape.

sentences.zh: 玄宗在蜀聞之，拜監察御史，會母喪，得風痺疾，客洪州，南北梗否，逾年詔命不至。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong in Shu heard of this and appointed him Investigating Censor; then his mother died. He contracted wind paralysis and lodged in Hongzhou; north and south were cut off, and for more than a year imperial orders did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong, then in Shu, heard of this and appointed him investigating censor; but his mother died, he contracted paralysis from wind-damp, and lodged in Hongzhou while north and south were cut off; more than a year passed without an imperial order reaching him.

sentences.zh: 有中人過州，頗求取無厭，南昌令王遘欲按之，謀於臯。

translations.literal: A palace envoy passed through the province and sought gain without limit; Magistrate Wang Sui of Nanchang wished to prosecute him and consulted with Gao.
translations.idiomatic: A palace envoy passed through the province and demanded bribes without end; Wang Sui, magistrate of Nanchang, wished to prosecute him and sought Gao's counsel.

sentences.zh: 臯良久不答，泣曰：「今何由致天子使，而遽欲治之！

translations.literal: Gao long did not answer, then wept: "How can we now summon an envoy of the Son of Heaven—and suddenly wish to punish him!"
translations.idiomatic: Gao was silent a long while, then wept and said: "How can we now summon an envoy of the Son of Heaven—and you would rush to punish him!"

sentences.zh: 」掩面去。

translations.literal: He covered his face and left.
translations.idiomatic: He covered his face and walked away.

sentences.zh: 遘悟，厚謝。

translations.literal: Sui understood, and thanked him lavishly.
translations.idiomatic: Sui understood and thanked him profusely.

sentences.zh: 浙西節度使顏真卿表為行軍司馬，召拜起居舍人，固辭。

translations.literal: Yan Zhenqing, Military Governor of Zhexi, memorialized him as Marching Sima; he was summoned as Attendant of the Heir Apparent, but firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhenqing, military governor of Zhexi, recommended him as marching sima; he was summoned as attendant of the heir apparent but firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「吾潔身亂世，以全吾誌，欲持是受名邪？

translations.literal: He once said: "I have kept my body pure in an age of chaos to preserve my aim—would I now take this post to receive a name for it?"
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "I have kept myself pure through an age of chaos to preserve my purpose—would I now accept office merely to win a reputation?"

sentences.zh: 」李季卿為江淮黜陟使，列其高行，以著作郎召，不就。

translations.literal: Li Jiqing as touring inspector of Jiang-Huai listed his lofty conduct and summoned him as Compiler of the Palace Library; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiqing, touring inspector of Jiang-Huai, commended his lofty conduct and summoned him as compiler of the Palace Library, but he would not accept.

sentences.zh: 自中原亂，士人率度江，李華、柳識、韓洄、王定皆仰臯節，與友善。

translations.literal: Since the central plains fell into chaos, scholar-officials mostly crossed the Yangzi; Li Hua, Liu Shi, Han Hui, and Wang Ding all looked up to Gao's integrity and befriended him.
translations.idiomatic: After the central plains fell into chaos, scholar-officials mostly fled south across the Yangzi; Li Hua, Liu Shi, Han Hui, and Wang Ding all revered Gao's integrity and became his friends.

sentences.zh: 洄、定常評臯可為宰輔、師保；

translations.literal: Hui and Ding often judged that Gao could serve as chief minister and tutor-protector.
translations.idiomatic: Hui and Ding often said that Gao was fit to serve as chief minister and royal tutor.

sentences.zh: 華亦以為分天下善惡，一人而已。

translations.literal: Hua also held that to divide the empire's good and evil required only this one man.
translations.idiomatic: Hua also held that to divide the empire's good and evil required only this one man.

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十六，洄等制服行哭，詔贈秘書少監。

translations.literal: He died at forty-six; Hui and the others wore mourning and went weeping; an edict enfeoffed him as Vice Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-six; Hui and the others wore mourning and followed the funeral procession weeping; an edict posthumously appointed him vice director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 元和中，謚為貞孝。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era he was given the posthumous title Upright and Filial.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe era he was given the posthumous title Upright and Filial.

sentences.zh: 子德輿，至宰相，別傳。

translations.literal: His son De-yu rose to Grand Councilor and has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Deyu rose to grand councilor and is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 甄濟，字孟成，定州無極人。

translations.literal: Zhen Ji, styled Mengcheng, was a native of Wuji in Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Ji, styled Mengcheng, was from Wuji in Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 叔父為幽、涼二州都督，家衛州，宗屬以伉俠相矜。

translations.literal: His uncle served as Military Governor of You and Liang prefectures; the family resided in Weizhou, and the clan prided itself on bold chivalry.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle had served as military governor of You and Liang; the family lived in Weizhou, and the clan prided itself on bold chivalry.

sentences.zh: 濟少孤，獨好學，以文雅稱。

translations.literal: Ji was orphaned young, loved learning alone, and was known for refined letters.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he devoted himself to learning and was known for refined scholarship.

sentences.zh: 居青巖山十餘年，遠近伏其仁，環山不敢畋漁。

translations.literal: He dwelt on Mount Qingyan for more than ten years; near and far submitted to his humanity, and for a circuit around the mountain none dared hunt or fish.
translations.idiomatic: He lived on Mount Qingyan for more than ten years; people near and far revered his humanity, and for miles around the mountain no one dared hunt or fish.

sentences.zh: 采訪使苗晉卿表之，諸府五辟，詔十至，堅臥不起。

translations.literal: Investigation Commissioner Miao Jinqing memorialized him; five prefectures summoned him; edicts came ten times, yet he lay abed and would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation commissioner Miao Jinqing recommended him; five prefectures invited him; imperial edicts arrived ten times, yet he steadfastly refused to leave his bed.

sentences.zh: 天寶十載，以左拾遺召，未至而安祿山入朝，求濟於玄宗，授范陽掌書記。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tianbao he was summoned as Left Reminder; before he arrived An Lushan came to court and begged Ji from Emperor Xuanzong, who appointed him Secretary of Fan-yang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Tianbao he was summoned as left reminder, but before he arrived An Lushan came to court and asked Xuanzong for Ji, who appointed him secretary of Fan-yang.

sentences.zh: 祿山至衛，使太守鄭遵意致謁山中，濟不得已為起，祿山下拜鈞禮。

translations.literal: When Lushan reached Wei, he had Prefect Zheng Zunyi go to the mountain to pay respects; Ji had no choice but to rise; Lushan bowed with the ceremony due an equal.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan reached Wei, he sent Prefect Zheng Zunyi to call on him in the mountains; Ji had no choice but to rise, and Lushan bowed to him with the ceremony due an equal.

sentences.zh: 居府中，論議正直。

translations.literal: Dwelling in the prefectural seat, his discussions were upright.
translations.idiomatic: While living at headquarters, his counsel was forthright and upright.

sentences.zh: 久之，察祿山有反謀，不可諫。

translations.literal: After a long while he perceived that Lushan harbored rebellion and could not be remonstrated with.
translations.idiomatic: In time he saw that Lushan was plotting rebellion and that remonstrance would be useless.

sentences.zh: 濟素善衛令齊玘，因謁歸，具告以誠。

translations.literal: Ji had long been friendly with Magistrate Qi Qi of Wei; he therefore went to pay respects and returned home, telling Qi everything in full sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Ji had long been on good terms with Wei magistrate Qi Qi; he paid his respects and returned home, telling Qi the whole truth.

sentences.zh: 密置羊血左右，至夜，若歐血狀，陽不支，舁歸舊廬。

translations.literal: He secretly placed sheep's blood beside him; at night he appeared to vomit blood, feigned collapse, and was carried back to his old hut.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly placed sheep's blood nearby; at night he feigned vomiting blood, pretended to collapse, and was carried back to his old dwelling.

sentences.zh: 祿山反，使蔡希德封刀召之，曰：「即不起，斷其頭見我。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled he sent Cai Xide with a sealed blade to summon him, saying: "If you still will not rise, cut off your head and bring it to me."
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rebelled he sent Cai Xide with a sealed blade to summon him, saying: "If you still refuse to come, cut off his head and bring it to me."

sentences.zh: 」濟色不動，左手書曰：「不可以行。

translations.literal: Ji's expression did not change; with his left hand he wrote: "Cannot go."
translations.idiomatic: Ji's expression never changed; with his left hand he wrote: "I cannot go."

sentences.zh: 」使者持刀趨前，濟引頸待之，希德歔欷嗟嘆，止刀，以實病告。

translations.literal: The envoy rushed forward with blade in hand; Ji stretched out his neck to await it. Xide sighed and wept, stayed the blade, and reported that the illness was real.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy rushed forward with his blade; Ji stretched out his neck to receive it. Xide sighed and wept, lowered the blade, and reported that Ji was truly ill.

sentences.zh: 後慶緒復使強輿至東都安國觀。

translations.literal: Later Qingxu again had him forcibly carried in a litter to the Anguo Abbey in the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qingxu again had him forcibly carried in a litter to the Anguo Abbey in the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 會廣平王平東都，濟詣軍門上謁泣涕，王為感動。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Guangping pacified the eastern capital, Ji went to the camp gate to pay respects in tears, and the prince was moved.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Guangping recaptured the eastern capital, Ji went to the camp gate in tears to pay his respects, and the prince was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 肅宗詔館之三司署，使汙賊官羅拜，以愧其心。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong ordered him lodged in the offices of the Three Departments and had defiled officials bow in ranks to shame his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong ordered him lodged in the offices of the Three Departments and had corrupted officials bow before him in ranks to shame them.

sentences.zh: 授秘書郎，或言太薄，更拜太子舍人。

translations.literal: He was appointed Secretary Gentleman; some said the rank was too low, so he was further appointed Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed secretary gentleman; some said the rank was too low, so he was further appointed attendant of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 來瑱辟為陜西襄陽參謀，拜禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: Lai Tian recruited him as staff officer of Xiangyang in Shanxi, and he was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Tian recruited him as staff officer for Xiangyang in Shanxi, and he was appointed vice director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 宜城楚昭王廟坎地廣九十畝，濟立墅其左。

translations.literal: The sunken ground beside the temple of King Zhao of Chu at Yicheng was ninety mu in extent; Ji built a villa to its left.
translations.idiomatic: Beside the temple of King Zhao of Chu at Yicheng lay sunken ground ninety mu in extent; Ji built a villa to the left of it.

sentences.zh: 瑱死，屏居七年。

translations.literal: When Tian died, he lived in seclusion for seven years.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian died, he lived in seclusion for seven years.

sentences.zh: 大歷初，江西節度使魏少遊表為著作郎，兼侍御史，卒。

translations.literal: In the early Dali era, Wei Shaoyou, Military Governor of Jiangxi, memorialized him as Compiler of the Palace Library and concurrently Investigating Censor; he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Dali era, Jiangxi military governor Wei Shaoyou recommended him as compiler of the Palace Library and concurrently investigating censor; he then died.

sentences.zh: 濟生子，因其官字曰禮闈、曰憲臺。

translations.literal: Ji had sons whom he styled by his offices: one called Liwai, one called Xiantai.
translations.idiomatic: Ji had sons whom he named after his offices: one he called Liwai, one Xiantai.

sentences.zh: 而禮闈死，憲臺更名逢，幼而孤。

translations.literal: Liwai died; Xiantai changed his name to Feng and was orphaned young.
translations.idiomatic: Liwai died; Xiantai changed his name to Feng and was orphaned while still young.

sentences.zh: 及長，耕宜城野，自力讀書，不謁州縣。

translations.literal: When he grew up he farmed the fields of Yicheng, studied on his own strength, and did not call on prefectural or county officials.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he farmed the fields around Yicheng, studied by his own labor, and never called on prefectural or county officials.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，節用以給親裏；

translations.literal: In years of famine he economized to supply kin and neighbors;
translations.idiomatic: In famine years he economized to supply his kin and neighbors;

sentences.zh: 大穰，則振其餘於鄉黨貧狹者。

translations.literal: when the harvest was abundant he distributed the surplus among the poor and narrow-minded in the village.
translations.idiomatic: when harvests were abundant he distributed the surplus among the poor of the village.

sentences.zh: 朋友有緩急，輒出家貲周贍，以義聞。

translations.literal: When friends were in urgent need he would bring out family wealth to support them, and became known for righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When friends were in need he would bring out family wealth to help them, and became known for his righteousness.

sentences.zh: 逢常以父名不得在國史，欲詣京師自言。

translations.literal: Feng often grieved that his father's name was not in the national histories and wished to go to the capital to speak for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Feng often grieved that his father's name was absent from the national histories and wished to go to the capital to plead his case.

sentences.zh: 元和中，袁滋表濟節行與權臯同科，宜載國史。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era Yuan Zi memorialized that Ji's integrity matched Quan Gao's and should be recorded in the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe era Yuan Zi memorialized that Ji's integrity equaled Quan Gao's and that he should be recorded in the national history.

sentences.zh: 有詔贈濟秘書少監。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously appointed Ji Vice Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously appointed Ji vice director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 而逢與元稹善，稹移書於史館修撰韓愈曰：「濟棄去祿山，及其反，有名號，又逼致之，執不起，卒不汙其名。

translations.literal: Feng was friendly with Yuan Zhen; Zhen wrote to Han Yu, compiler at the History Office, saying: "Ji abandoned Lushan's service; when Lushan rebelled he had a title, and though they forced him to come he would not rise and in the end did not stain his name."
translations.idiomatic: Feng was friendly with Yuan Zhen; Zhen wrote to Han Yu at the History Office, saying: "Ji left Lushan's service; when Lushan rebelled he bore an office title, and though they forced him to come he would not rise and never stained his name."

sentences.zh: 夫辨所從於居易之時，堅其操於利仁之世，而猶選懦者之所不為，蓋怫人之心難，而害己之避深也。

translations.literal: To discern whom to follow in a time when principle is easy to change, and to hold fast to one's integrity in an age that favors profit and benevolence—yet this is what the timid dare not do, for it offends men's hearts and the harm one avoids for oneself runs deep.
translations.idiomatic: To choose whom to follow when principle is easy to abandon, and to hold fast to one's integrity in an age that favors profit and kindness—this is what the timid dare not do, for it offends men's hearts and the harm one avoids for oneself runs deep.

sentences.zh: 至天下大亂，死忠者不必顯，從亂者不必誅，而眷眷本朝，甘心白刃，難矣哉！

translations.literal: When the empire falls into great chaos, those who die loyal need not be made famous, and those who follow rebellion need not be punished—yet to cling to the native dynasty and willingly face the white blade is hard indeed!
translations.idiomatic: When the empire falls into great chaos, those who die loyal need not be honored, and those who follow rebellion need not be punished—yet to cling to the native dynasty and willingly face the blade is hard indeed!

sentences.zh: 若甄生，弁冕不加其身，祿食不進其口，直布衣一男子耳。

translations.literal: As for Master Zhen, cap and robes never touched his person, salary and food never entered his mouth—he was only a plain-clothed man.
translations.idiomatic: As for Master Zhen, cap and robes never touched his person, salary and food never entered his mouth—he was only a man in plain cloth.

sentences.zh: 及亂，則延頸受刃，分死不回，不以不必顯而廢忠，不以不必誅而從亂。

translations.literal: When chaos came he stretched out his neck to receive the blade and would not turn from death; he did not abandon loyalty because fame was not assured, nor follow rebellion because punishment was not assured.
translations.idiomatic: When chaos came he stretched out his neck to receive the blade and would not turn back; he did not abandon loyalty because fame was uncertain, nor follow rebellion because punishment was uncertain.

sentences.zh: 在古與今，蓋百一焉。

translations.literal: In antiquity and in the present, such men are perhaps one in a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity and in the present, such men are perhaps one in a hundred.

sentences.zh: 」愈答曰：「逢能行身，幸於方州大臣，以標目其先人事，載之天下耳目，徹之天子，追爵其父第四品，赫然驚人，逢與其父俱當得書矣。

translations.literal: Yu replied: "Feng can act in his own person; fortunate in a regional grandee, he made his forebear's deeds known to the empire's eyes and reached the Son of Heaven; his father was posthumously enfeoffed at the fourth rank, startling all men. Both Feng and his father deserve to be written."
translations.idiomatic: Yu replied: "Feng acted in his own person; fortunate in a regional grandee, he brought his forebear's deeds before the empire's eyes and reached the Son of Heaven; his father was posthumously enfeoffed at the fourth rank, startling all men. Both Feng and his father deserve to be written."

sentences.zh: 」由是父子俱顯名。

translations.literal: "Thus father and son both became renowned."
translations.idiomatic: "Thus father and son both won lasting fame."

sentences.zh: 陽城，字亢宗，定州北平人，徙陜州夏縣，世為官族。

translations.literal: Yang Cheng, styled Kangzong, was a native of Beiping in Dingzhou, moved to Xia County in Shanzhou, and for generations was an official clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Cheng, styled Kangzong, was from Beiping in Dingzhou and later moved to Xia County in Shanzhou; his family had served as officials for generations.

sentences.zh: 資好學，貧不能得書，求為吏，隸集賢院，竊院書讀之，晝夜不出戶，六年，無所不通。

translations.literal: Though he loved learning, he was too poor to obtain books; he sought to become a clerk, entered service at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, stole books from the hall to read, and for six years did not leave his door, until there was nothing he did not understand.
translations.idiomatic: Though he loved learning, poverty kept him from books; he sought work as a clerk at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, stole books from the hall to read, and for six years never left his door until he had mastered everything.

sentences.zh: 及進士第，乃去隱中條山，與弟堦、域常易衣出。

translations.literal: After passing the jinshi he left and hid on Mount Zhongtiao, often changing clothes with his younger brothers Jie and Yu when going out.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi he withdrew to Mount Zhongtiao, often changing clothes with his younger brothers Jie and Yu when they went out.

sentences.zh: 年長，不肯娶，謂弟曰：「吾與若孤煢相育，既娶則間外姓，雖共處而益疏，我不忍。

translations.literal: When he grew older he would not marry, and told his brothers: "You and I have reared one another in orphan solitude; once we marry, outside surnames come between us; though we dwell together we grow more distant—I cannot bear it."
translations.idiomatic: As he grew older he refused to marry and told his brothers: "You and I have raised one another in lonely orphanhood; once we marry, outsiders come between us; though we live together we grow apart—I cannot bear it."

sentences.zh: 」弟義之，亦不娶，遂終身。

translations.literal: His brothers agreed and likewise did not marry, and so remained unmarried all their lives.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers agreed and likewise never married, remaining so all their lives.

sentences.zh: 城謙恭簡素，遇人長幼如一。

translations.literal: Cheng was modest, respectful, and plain; toward people old and young he was the same.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was modest, respectful, and plain; toward people old and young he was always the same.

sentences.zh: 遠近慕其行，來學者跡接於道。

translations.literal: Near and far admired his conduct, and those who came to study left footprints continuous along the road.
translations.idiomatic: Near and far admired his conduct, and learners' footprints lined the road unbroken.

sentences.zh: 閭里有爭訟，不詣官而詣城決之。

translations.literal: When neighbors had disputes they did not go to officials but came to Cheng to decide them.
translations.idiomatic: When neighbors quarreled they did not go to the magistrate but came to Cheng for judgment.

sentences.zh: 有盜其樹者，城遇之，慮其恥，退自匿。

translations.literal: When someone stole his trees, Cheng met him and, fearing his shame, withdrew and hid himself.
translations.idiomatic: When someone stole his trees, Cheng met him but, fearing to shame him, withdrew and hid.

sentences.zh: 嘗絕糧，遣奴求米，奴以米易酒，醉臥於路。

translations.literal: Once he ran out of grain and sent a slave to fetch rice; the slave traded the rice for wine and lay drunk on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Once he ran out of grain and sent a slave to fetch rice; the slave traded the rice for wine and lay drunk in the road.

sentences.zh: 城怪其故，與弟迎之，奴未醒，乃負以歸。

translations.literal: Cheng wondered at the delay and went with his brother to meet him; the slave had not yet awakened, so they carried him home on their backs.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng wondered at the delay and went with his brother to meet him; the slave had not yet awakened, so they carried him home on their backs.

sentences.zh: 及覺，痛咎謝，城曰：「寒而飲，何責焉？

translations.literal: When he awoke he reproached himself bitterly and apologized; Cheng said: "You drank because you were cold—what blame is there?"
translations.idiomatic: When the slave awoke he reproached himself bitterly; Cheng said: "You drank because you were cold—what fault is that?"

sentences.zh: 」寡妹依城居，其子四十餘，癡不知人，城常負以出入。

translations.literal: A widowed younger sister lived with Cheng; her son was more than forty, an idiot who knew no one, yet Cheng often carried him when going out.
translations.idiomatic: A widowed younger sister lived with Cheng; her son was past forty, feeble-minded and knowing no one, yet Cheng often carried him when he went out.

sentences.zh: 始，妹之夫客死遠方，城與弟行千里，負其柩歸葬。

translations.literal: At first her husband had died as a guest far away; Cheng and his brother traveled a thousand li and carried the coffin home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: At first her husband had died far from home; Cheng and his brother traveled a thousand li and carried the coffin home for burial.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，屏跡不過鄰裏，屑榆為粥，講論不輟。

translations.literal: In years of famine he kept his traces from crossing even the neighboring lanes, ground elm bark into porridge, and never ceased his lectures.
translations.idiomatic: In famine years he would not even cross to neighboring lanes, ground elm bark into porridge, and never ceased his lectures.

sentences.zh: 有奴都兒化其德，亦方介自約。

translations.literal: A slave named Du'er was transformed by his virtue and likewise held himself to strict self-restraint.
translations.idiomatic: A slave named Du'er was transformed by his virtue and likewise held himself to strict restraint.

sentences.zh: 或哀其餒，與之食，不納。

translations.literal: When some pitied his hunger and offered him food, he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When some pitied his hunger and offered him food, he would not accept.

sentences.zh: 後致糠核數杯，乃受。

translations.literal: Later they brought several cups of chaff and grain; only then did he accept.
translations.idiomatic: Later they brought a few cups of chaff and grain; only then did he accept.

sentences.zh: 山東節度府聞城義者，發使遺五百縑，戒使者不令返。

translations.literal: The eastern circuit military headquarters heard of Cheng's righteousness and sent an envoy with five hundred bolts of silk, instructing the envoy not to return.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern circuit headquarters heard of Cheng's righteousness and sent an envoy with five hundred bolts of silk, ordering him not to return.

sentences.zh: 城固辭，使者委而去，城置之未嘗發。

translations.literal: Cheng firmly declined; the envoy left it and departed; Cheng set it aside and never opened it.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng firmly declined; the envoy left the silk and departed; Cheng set it aside and never opened it.

sentences.zh: 會里人鄭俶欲葬親，貸於人無得，城知其然，舉縑與之。

translations.literal: When a neighbor, Zheng Chu, wished to bury his kin but could borrow from no one, Cheng, knowing this, gave him all the silk.
translations.idiomatic: When his neighbor Zheng Chu wished to bury his kin but could borrow from no one, Cheng, knowing this, gave him all the silk.

sentences.zh: 俶既葬，還曰：「蒙君子之施，願為奴以償德。

translations.literal: After the burial Chu returned and said: "I received the gentleman's gift and wish to become your slave to repay this virtue."
translations.idiomatic: After the burial Chu returned and said: "I have received the gentleman's kindness and wish to become your slave to repay it."

sentences.zh: 」城曰：「吾子非也，能同我為學乎？

translations.literal: Cheng said: "You are not that sort of man—can you study together with me?"
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said: "You are not that sort of man—will you study together with me?"

sentences.zh: 」俶泣謝，即教以書，俶不能業，城更徙遠阜，使顓其習。

translations.literal: Chu wept and thanked him; Cheng thereupon taught him to write. Chu could not master it, so Cheng moved farther to a remote hill and had him focus on his studies.
translations.idiomatic: Chu wept and thanked him; Cheng taught him to write. When Chu could not master it, Cheng moved him to a remote hill and had him focus on his studies.

sentences.zh: 學如初，慚，縊而死。

translations.literal: His studies were as before; ashamed, he hanged himself and died.
translations.idiomatic: His progress was still as before; ashamed, he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 城驚且哭，厚自咎，為服緦麻瘞之。

translations.literal: Cheng was startled and wept, blamed himself deeply, wore the hemp of mourning, and buried him.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was startled and wept, blamed himself deeply, wore mourning hemp, and buried him.

sentences.zh: 陜虢觀察使李泌數禮餉，城受之。

translations.literal: Li Mi, Observation Commissioner of Shan-Guo, often sent gifts of food, and Cheng accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi, observation commissioner of Shan-Guo, often sent him gifts of food, which Cheng accepted.

sentences.zh: 泌欲辟致之府，不起，乃薦諸朝，詔以著作佐郎召，並賜緋魚。

translations.literal: Mi wished to summon him to his headquarters but he would not go; Mi then recommended him to court, and an edict summoned him as Assistant Compiler with crimson robe and fish tally bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Mi wished to summon him to headquarters but he would not go; Mi then recommended him to court, and an edict summoned him as assistant compiler, bestowing crimson robe and fish tally.

sentences.zh: 泌使參軍事韓傑奉詔至其家，城封還詔，自稱「多病老憊，不堪奔奉，惟哀憐」。

translations.literal: Mi sent his staff officer Han Jie to deliver the edict to his home; Cheng sealed and returned the edict, saying of himself: "Much ill and old exhaustion—I cannot hasten to serve; only beg compassion."
translations.idiomatic: Mi sent staff officer Han Jie to deliver the edict to his home; Cheng sealed and returned the edict, writing: "Much ill and old exhaustion—I cannot hasten to serve; only beg compassion."

sentences.zh: 泌不敢強。

translations.literal: Mi did not dare press him.
translations.idiomatic: Mi did not dare press him.

sentences.zh: 及為宰相，又言之德宗，於是召拜右諫議大夫，遣長安尉楊寧賫束帛詣其家。

translations.literal: When he became chief minister he again spoke of him to Dezong; Cheng was then summoned as Right Remonstrator, and Chang'an Magistrate Yang Ning was sent with silks to his home.
translations.idiomatic: When Mi became chief minister he again spoke of Cheng to Emperor Dezong; Cheng was then summoned as right remonstrator, and Chang'an magistrate Yang Ning was sent with silks to his home.

sentences.zh: 城褐衣到闕下辭讓，帝遣中人持緋衣衣之，召見，賜帛五十匹。

translations.literal: Cheng came to court in brown clothes to decline; the emperor sent a eunuch to clothe him in crimson and summoned him, bestowing fifty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng came to court in brown clothes to decline; the emperor sent a eunuch to clothe him in crimson and summoned him, bestowing fifty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 初，城未起，縉紳想見風采。

translations.literal: At first, before Cheng rose from seclusion, the gentry longed to see his bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Before Cheng left seclusion, the gentry longed to see his bearing.

sentences.zh: 既興草茅，處諫諍官，士以為且死職，天下益憚之。

translations.literal: Once raised from the thatched hut to the office of remonstrance, scholars thought he would die in his post, and the empire feared him still more.
translations.idiomatic: Once raised from humble seclusion to remonstrator, scholars thought he would die in his post, and the empire feared him all the more.

sentences.zh: 及受命，它諫官論事苛細紛紛，帝厭苦，而城浸聞得失且熟，猶未肯言。

translations.literal: After he took office, other remonstrators debated matters in petty detail; the emperor grew weary, while Cheng gradually heard gains and losses and knew them well, yet still would not speak.
translations.idiomatic: After he took office, other remonstrators debated petty details until the emperor grew weary; Cheng gradually heard all gains and losses and knew them well, yet still would not speak.

sentences.zh: 韓愈作《爭臣論》譏切之，城不屑。

translations.literal: Han Yu wrote "On Remonstrating Ministers" to rebuke him sharply; Cheng paid it no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu wrote "On Remonstrating Ministers" to rebuke him sharply; Cheng paid it no heed.

sentences.zh: 方與二弟延賓客，日夜劇飲。

translations.literal: He was then entertaining guests with his two younger brothers, drinking heavily day and night.
translations.idiomatic: He was then entertaining guests with his two younger brothers, drinking heavily day and night.

sentences.zh: 客欲諫止者，城揣知其情，強飲客，客辭，即自引滿，客不得已。

translations.literal: When guests wished to remonstrate and stop him, Cheng guessed their intent and forced them to drink; when guests declined he would fill his own cup; guests had no choice.
translations.idiomatic: When guests wished to remonstrate, Cheng guessed their intent and forced them to drink; when they declined he filled his own cup until they had no choice.

sentences.zh: 與酬酢，或醉，仆席上，城或先醉臥客懷中，不能聽客語，無得關言。

translations.literal: They drank in turn; some grew drunk and fell on the mat; Cheng sometimes grew drunk first and lay in a guest's lap, unable to hear the guest's words, so none could get a word in.
translations.idiomatic: They drank in turn; some fell drunk on the mat; Cheng sometimes grew drunk first and lay in a guest's lap, unable to hear their words, so none could intervene.

sentences.zh: 常以木枕布衾質錢，人重其賢，爭售之。

translations.literal: He often pawned his wooden pillow and cloth quilt for cash; people prized his worth and vied to buy them.
translations.idiomatic: He often pawned his wooden pillow and cloth quilt; people prized his virtue and vied to buy them.

sentences.zh: 每約二弟：「吾所俸入，而可度月食米幾何，薪菜鹽幾錢，先具之，余送酒家，無留也。

translations.literal: He often agreed with his two younger brothers: "From my salary, how much rice can we eat in a month, how much for fuel, vegetables, and salt—prepare that first; the rest goes to the wine shop; keep none."
translations.idiomatic: He often told his brothers: "From my salary, figure how much rice we need for a month, how much for fuel, vegetables, and salt—prepare that first; send the rest to the wine shop and keep none."

sentences.zh: 」服用無贏副，客或稱其佳可愛，輒喜，舉授之。

translations.literal: He had no spare clothing; when guests praised something he wore as fine and lovable, he would gladly give it away.
translations.idiomatic: He kept no spare clothing; when guests praised something he wore, he would gladly give it away.

sentences.zh: 有陳萇者，候其得俸，常往稱錢之美，月有獲焉。

translations.literal: There was a Chen Chang who, whenever Cheng received his salary, would come praising the beauty of the cash and each month gained something.
translations.idiomatic: There was a Chen Chang who, whenever Cheng received his salary, would come praising the beauty of the cash and each month gained something from him.

sentences.zh: 居位八年，人不能窺其際。

translations.literal: He held office eight years and no one could fathom his inner mind.
translations.idiomatic: He held office eight years, and no one could fathom his inner mind.

sentences.zh: 及裴延齡誣逐陸贄、張滂、李充等，帝怒甚，無敢言。

translations.literal: When Pei Yanling falsely drove out Lu Zan, Zhang Pang, Li Chong, and others, the emperor was furious beyond measure and none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Yanling falsely drove out Lu Zan, Zhang Pang, Li Chong, and others, the emperor was furious beyond measure and none dared speak.

sentences.zh: 城聞，曰：「吾諫官，不可令天子殺無罪大臣。

translations.literal: When Cheng heard this he said: "I am a remonstrator—I cannot let the Son of Heaven kill guiltless chief ministers."
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng heard this he said: "I am a remonstrator—I cannot let the Son of Heaven kill guiltless chief ministers."

sentences.zh: 」乃約拾遺王仲舒守延英閣上疏極論延齡罪，慷慨引誼，申直贄等，累日不止。

translations.literal: He then joined Reminder Wang Zhongshu in guarding the Yanying Pavilion to submit a memorial vehemently denouncing Yanling's crimes, speaking with passionate righteousness and defending Zan and the others straightly, for days without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined reminder Wang Zhongshu in guarding the Yanying Pavilion to submit a memorial fiercely denouncing Yanling's crimes, speaking with passionate righteousness and defending Zan and the others, for days without cease.

sentences.zh: 聞者寒懼，城愈勵。

translations.literal: Hearers shivered in fear, yet Cheng pressed all the harder.
translations.idiomatic: Hearers shivered in fear, yet Cheng pressed all the harder.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，召宰相抵城罪。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and summoned the chief ministers to reproach Cheng's offense.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly enraged and summoned the chief ministers to reproach Cheng.

sentences.zh: 順宗方為皇太子，為開救，良久得免，敕宰相諭遣。

translations.literal: Shunzong was then heir apparent and interceded for him; after a long while Cheng was spared; the emperor ordered the chief ministers to admonish and send him away.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzong was then heir apparent and interceded; after a long while Cheng was spared; the emperor ordered the chief ministers to admonish and dismiss him.

sentences.zh: 然帝意不已，欲遂相延齡。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor's intent was not finished; he still wished to make Yanling chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor's intent was not finished; he still wished to make Yanling chief minister.

sentences.zh: 城顯語曰：「延齡為相，吾當取白麻壞之，哭於廷。

translations.literal: Cheng said openly: "If Yanling becomes chief minister, I shall take the white hemp edict and tear it, and weep in the court."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said openly: "If Yanling becomes chief minister, I shall seize the white hemp edict of appointment, tear it, and weep in the court."

sentences.zh: 」帝不相延齡，城力也。

translations.literal: The emperor did not make Yanling chief minister—Cheng's force accomplished it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not make Yanling chief minister—Cheng's force accomplished it.

sentences.zh: 坐是下遷國子司業。

translations.literal: For this he was demoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was demoted to vice director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 引諸生告之曰：「凡學者，所以學為忠與孝也。

translations.literal: He gathered the students and told them: "All who study do so to learn loyalty and filial piety."
translations.idiomatic: He gathered the students and told them: "All who study do so to learn loyalty and filial piety."

sentences.zh: 諸生有久不省親者乎？

translations.literal: "Are there students who have long failed to visit their parents?"
translations.idiomatic: "Are there students who have long failed to visit their parents?"

sentences.zh: 」明日謁城還養者二十輩，有三年不歸侍者，斥之。

translations.literal: The next day twenty who came to Cheng to return home to care for parents; those who had not attended parents for three years he expelled.
translations.idiomatic: The next day twenty came to Cheng to return home and care for their parents; those who had not attended their parents for three years he expelled.

sentences.zh: 簡孝秀德行升堂上，沈酗不率教者皆罷。

translations.literal: He selected the filial, the worthy, and those of fine conduct to ascend to the hall; those sunk in drink and disobedient to teaching were all dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He selected the filial, worthy, and well-conducted to ascend to the hall; those sunk in drink and disobedient to teaching were all dismissed.

sentences.zh: 躬講經籍，生徒斤斤皆有法度。

translations.literal: He personally lectured on the classics, and the students were all orderly and within rule.
translations.idiomatic: He personally lectured on the classics, and the students were all orderly and within rule.

sentences.zh: 薛約者，狂而直，言事得罪，謫連州。

translations.literal: Xue Yue was wild and blunt; remonstrating on affairs he offended and was demoted to Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yue was wild and blunt; remonstrating on affairs he gave offense and was demoted to Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 吏捕跡，得之城家。

translations.literal: Officers pursued his tracks and found him in Cheng's house.
translations.idiomatic: Officers pursued his tracks and found him at Cheng's house.

sentences.zh: 城坐吏於門，引約飲食訖，步至都外與別。

translations.literal: Cheng seated the officer at the gate, saw Yue finish eating and drinking, then walked with him outside the capital to bid farewell.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng seated the officer at the gate, saw Yue finish eating and drinking, then walked with him outside the capital to bid farewell.

sentences.zh: 帝惡城黨有罪，出為道州刺史，太學諸生何蕃、季償、王魯卿、李讜等二百人頓首闕下，請留城。

translations.literal: The emperor hated that Cheng harbored a guilty man and sent him out as prefect of Daozhou; more than two hundred students of the Imperial University—He Fan, Ji Chang, Wang Luqing, Li Dan, and others—knelt at the palace gate begging that Cheng be kept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hated that Cheng harbored a guilty man and sent him out as prefect of Daozhou; more than two hundred Imperial University students—He Fan, Ji Chang, Wang Luqing, Li Dan, and others—knelt at the palace gate begging that Cheng be kept.

sentences.zh: 柳宗元聞之，遺蕃等書曰：「詔出陽公道州，仆聞悒然。

translations.literal: Liu Zongyuan heard of this and sent Fan and the others a letter saying: "An edict has sent Master Yang to Daozhou; on hearing it I am deeply grieved."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zongyuan heard of this and sent Fan and the others a letter saying: "An edict has sent Master Yang to Daozhou; on hearing it I am deeply grieved."

sentences.zh: 幸生不諱之代，不能論列大體，聞下執事，還陽公之南也。

translations.literal: Fortunate to live in an age without taboo, I cannot set forth the larger pattern; hearing that your office is sending Master Yang back south.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunate to live in an age without taboo, I cannot set forth the larger pattern; I hear that your office is sending Master Yang back south.

sentences.zh: 今諸生愛慕陽公德，懇悃乞留，輒用撫手喜甚。

translations.literal: Now the students love and admire Master Yang's virtue and earnestly beg that he be kept; I clap my hands in great joy.
translations.idiomatic: Now the students love Master Yang's virtue and earnestly beg that he be kept; I clap my hands in great joy.

sentences.zh: 昔李膺、嵇康時，太學生徒仰闕執訴，仆謂訖千百年不可復見，乃在今日，誠諸生見賜甚厚，將亦陽公漸漬導訓所致乎！

translations.literal: In the days of Li Ying and Ji Kang, Imperial University students looked up to the palace gate and pleaded their case; I thought that after a thousand years this could not be seen again—yet it is before us today. Truly the students have shown me great kindness; is this not also the gradual guidance and instruction of Master Yang!
translations.idiomatic: In the days of Li Ying and Ji Kang, university students looked up to the palace gate and pleaded their case; I thought that after a thousand years one would never see this again—yet here it is today. The students have shown me great kindness; is this not also the gradual teaching of Master Yang!

sentences.zh: 噫！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 公有博厚恢大之德，並容善偽，來者不拒。

translations.literal: The Master has broad, thick, and expansive virtue, embracing both the good and the false, and does not reject those who come.
translations.idiomatic: The Master has broad and expansive virtue, embracing both the worthy and the unworthy, and does not turn away those who come.

sentences.zh: 有狂惑小生，依托門下，飛文陳愚。

translations.literal: There is a wild and deluded young man who relies on his gate and sends flying letters stating foolishness.
translations.idiomatic: There is a wild and deluded young man who clings to his gate and sends reckless letters full of folly.

sentences.zh: 論者以為陽公過於納汙，無人師道。

translations.literal: Critics hold that Master Yang accepts the filthy too readily and lacks the way of a teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Critics say Master Yang accepts the unworthy too readily and lacks the way of a true teacher.

sentences.zh: 仲尼吾黨狂狷，南郭獻譏；

translations.literal: Confucius had the wild and the narrow among his party; Nan Guo offered mockery;
translations.idiomatic: Confucius had the wild and the narrow among his followers; Nan Guo offered mockery;

sentences.zh: 曾參徒七十二人，致禍負芻；

translations.literal: Zeng Shen had seventy-two disciples and brought disaster carrying straw;
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Shen had seventy-two disciples and brought disaster carrying straw;

sentences.zh: 孟軻館齊，從者竊屨。

translations.literal: Meng Ke lodged in Qi and a follower stole shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Mencius lodged in Qi and a follower stole shoes.

sentences.zh: 彼聖賢猶不免，如之何其拒人也？

translations.literal: Even those sages could not avoid such things—how then can one reject people?
translations.idiomatic: Even those sages could not avoid such things—how then can one reject people?

sentences.zh: 俞、扁之門，不拒病夫；

translations.literal: At the gates of Bian Que and Chunyu Yi they did not reject the sick;
translations.idiomatic: At the gates of Bian Que and Chunyu Yi they did not reject the sick;

sentences.zh: 繩墨之側，不拒枉材；

translations.literal: Beside the carpenter's line they did not reject crooked timber;
translations.idiomatic: Beside the carpenter's line they did not reject crooked timber;

sentences.zh: 師儒之席，不拒曲士。

translations.literal: At the teacher's mat they did not reject the twisted scholar.
translations.idiomatic: At the teacher's mat they did not reject the twisted scholar.

sentences.zh: 且陽公在朝，四方聞風，貪冒茍進邪薄之夫沮其志，雖微師尹之位，而人實瞻望焉。

translations.literal: Moreover, while Master Yang is at court, all four quarters hear his wind; greedy, reckless, base men who advance by evil ways would be checked in their intent; though he lacks the rank of chief minister, men truly look up to him.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, while Master Yang is at court, all four quarters hear his influence; greedy and base men who advance by evil ways would be checked in their intent; though he lacks a chief minister's rank, men truly look up to him.

sentences.zh: 與其化一州，其功遠近可量哉！

translations.literal: To transform one whole prefecture—how far might that achievement reach!
translations.idiomatic: To transform a whole prefecture—how far might that achievement reach!

sentences.zh: 諸生之言，非獨為己也，於國甚宜。

translations.literal: The students' words are not for themselves alone; they are very fitting for the state.
translations.idiomatic: The students' words are not for themselves alone; they are very fitting for the state.

sentences.zh: 」蕃等守闕下數日，為吏遮抑不得上。

translations.literal: Fan and the others guarded the palace gate for several days but were held back by officers and could not ascend.
translations.idiomatic: Fan and the others waited at the palace gate for several days but were held back by officers and could not get through.

sentences.zh: 既行，皆泣涕，立石紀德。

translations.literal: When he departed, all wept; they erected a stone to record his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When he departed, all wept; they erected a stone to record his virtue.

sentences.zh: 至道州，治民如治家，宜罰罰之，宜賞賞之，不以簿書介意。

translations.literal: At Daozhou he governed the people as he would his own household: whom he should punish he punished, whom he should reward he rewarded, and he did not trouble himself over documents and registers.
translations.idiomatic: At Daozhou he governed the people as he would his own household: whom he should punish he punished, whom he should reward he rewarded, without troubling himself over documents and registers.

sentences.zh: 月俸取足則已，官收其餘。

translations.literal: He took only enough from his monthly salary and let the office keep the rest.
translations.idiomatic: He took only enough from his monthly salary and let the office keep the rest.

sentences.zh: 日炊米二斛，魚一大，置甌杓道上，人共食之。

translations.literal: Each day he cooked two hu of rice and one large fish, set bowls and ladles on the road, and all shared the food.
translations.idiomatic: Each day he cooked two hu of rice and one large fish, set bowls and ladles on the road, and all shared the meal.

sentences.zh: 州產侏儒，歲貢諸朝，城哀其生離，無所進。

translations.literal: The prefecture produced dwarfs who were sent yearly as tribute to court; Cheng grieved that they were torn from their lives and had nowhere to advance.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture produced dwarfs sent yearly as tribute to court; Cheng grieved that they were torn from home and had nowhere to go.

sentences.zh: 帝使求之，城奏曰：「州民盡短，若以貢，不知何者可供。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered them sought; Cheng memorialized: "The people of this prefecture are all short; if we must send tribute, I do not know who can be supplied.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered them sought; Cheng memorialized: "The people of this prefecture are all short; if tribute is required, I do not know who can be supplied.

sentences.zh: 」自是罷。

translations.literal: From this the practice ceased.
translations.idiomatic: From this the practice ceased.

sentences.zh: 州人感之，以「陽」名子。

translations.literal: The people of the prefecture were moved and named their sons "Yang."
translations.idiomatic: The people were moved and named their sons Yang.

sentences.zh: 前刺史坐罪下獄，吏有幸於刺史者，拾不法事告城，欲自脫，城輒搒殺之。

translations.literal: The former prefect had been imprisoned for a crime; a clerk who had been favored by the prefect picked out unlawful matters to report against Cheng, wishing to save himself; Cheng had him beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: The former prefect had been imprisoned for a crime; a clerk favored by the prefect picked out unlawful matters to report against Cheng, wishing to save himself; Cheng had him beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 賦稅不時，觀察使數誚責。

translations.literal: Taxes were not paid on time and the observation commissioner repeatedly rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes were not paid on time and the observation commissioner repeatedly rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 州當上考功第，城自署曰：「撫字心勞，追科政拙，考下下。

translations.literal: The prefecture should have ranked highest in merit evaluation; Cheng wrote on his own report: "My heart labored in nurturing the people, my policy in pursuing collections was clumsy—grade: lowest."
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture should have ranked highest in merit evaluation; Cheng wrote on his own report: "My heart labored in nurturing the people, my policy in pursuing collections was clumsy—grade: lowest."

sentences.zh: 」觀察府遣判官督賦，至州，怪城不迎，以問吏，吏曰：「刺史以為有罪，自囚於獄。

translations.literal: The observation office sent an aide to supervise tax collection; arriving at the prefecture he wondered that Cheng did not come to meet him and asked the clerks; the clerks said: "The prefect thinks himself guilty and has imprisoned himself in jail.
translations.idiomatic: The observation office sent an aide to supervise tax collection; arriving at the prefecture he wondered that Cheng did not come to meet him and asked the clerks; they said: "The prefect thinks himself guilty and has imprisoned himself in jail.

sentences.zh: 」判官驚，馳入，謁城曰：「使君何罪？

translations.literal: The aide was startled, rushed in, and paid respects to Cheng, saying: "What crime has the prefect committed?"
translations.idiomatic: The aide was startled, rushed in, and paid respects to Cheng, saying: "What crime has the prefect committed?"

sentences.zh: 我奉命來候安否耳。

translations.literal: I am ordered only to inquire after your well-being."
translations.idiomatic: I am ordered only to inquire after your well-being."

sentences.zh: 」留數日，城不敢歸，仆門闔，寢館外以待命。

translations.literal: He stayed several days; Cheng dared not return home, lay prostrate at the gate, and slept outside the guest quarters awaiting orders.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed several days; Cheng dared not return home, lay prostrate at the gate, and slept outside the guest quarters awaiting orders.

sentences.zh: 判官遽辭去。

translations.literal: The aide hurriedly took his leave.
translations.idiomatic: The aide hurriedly took his leave.

sentences.zh: 府復遣官來按舉，義不欲行，乃載妻子中道逃去。

translations.literal: The office again sent an officer to investigate; unwilling in principle to go, he loaded wife and children and fled midway.
translations.idiomatic: The office again sent an officer to investigate; unwilling in principle to go, he loaded wife and children and fled midway.

sentences.zh: 順宗立，召還城，而城已卒，年七十，贈左散騎常侍，賜其家錢二十萬，官護喪歸葬。

translations.literal: When Shunzong ascended the throne he summoned Cheng back, but Cheng had already died at seventy; he was posthumously appointed Left Regular Cavalryman, his household was given two hundred thousand cash, and officials escorted the coffin home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong ascended the throne he summoned Cheng back, but Cheng had already died at seventy; he was posthumously appointed left regular cavalryman, his household was given two hundred thousand cash, and officials escorted the coffin home for burial.

sentences.zh: 蕃，和州人。

translations.literal: Fan was a man of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was from Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 事父母孝。

translations.literal: He served his parents with filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He served his parents with filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 學太學，歲一歸，父母不許。

translations.literal: Studying at the Imperial University, he returned once a year but his parents would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Studying at the Imperial University, he returned once a year but his parents would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 間二歲乃歸，復不許。

translations.literal: Only after two years did he return, and again they would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Only after two years did he return, and again they would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 凡五歲，慨然以親且老，不自安，揖諸生去，乃共閉蕃空舍中，眾共狀蕃義行，白城請留。

translations.literal: After five years he sighed that his parents were growing old and he could not be at ease; he bowed to the students and left; they together shut Fan in an empty room; all jointly petitioned Fan's righteous conduct and reported to Cheng asking that he be kept.
translations.idiomatic: After five years he sighed that his parents were growing old and he could not be at ease; he bowed to the students and left; they shut Fan in an empty room; all jointly petitioned his righteous conduct and asked Cheng to keep him.

sentences.zh: 會城罷，亦止。

translations.literal: When Cheng was dismissed, this also ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng was dismissed, this also ceased.

sentences.zh: 初，朱泚反，諸生將從亂，蕃正色叱不聽，故六館士無受汙者。

translations.literal: At first, when Zhu Ci rebelled, the students were about to follow the rebellion; Fan sternly rebuked them and they would not listen, so none of the six halls' scholars were defiled.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled, the students were about to follow the rebellion; Fan sternly rebuked them until they desisted, so none of the six halls' scholars were defiled.

sentences.zh: 蕃居太學二十年，有死喪無歸者，皆身為治喪。

translations.literal: Fan dwelt at the Imperial University twenty years; when any died with no kin to return the body, he personally arranged the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Fan dwelt at the Imperial University twenty years; when any died with no kin to return the body, he personally arranged the funeral.

sentences.zh: 償，魯人。
