translations.literal: Chang was a man of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Chang was from Lu.

sentences.zh: 魯卿，第進士，有名。

translations.literal: Lu Qing passed the jinshi and was renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Luqing passed the jinshi and was renowned.

sentences.zh: 司空圖

translations.literal: Sikong Tu
translations.idiomatic: Sikong Tu

sentences.zh: 司空圖，字表聖，河中虞鄉人。

translations.literal: Sikong Tu, styled Biaosheng, was a native of Yuxiang in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Sikong Tu, styled Biaosheng, was from Yuxiang in Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 父輿，有風幹。

translations.literal: His father Yu had presence and force of character.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu had presence and force of character.

sentences.zh: 當大中時，盧弘正管鹽鐵，表為安邑兩池榷鹽使。

translations.literal: In the Dazhong era, when Lu Hongzheng managed the Salt Monopoly, he memorialized Yu as Commissioner of the Monopoly Salt at the Two Pools of Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dazhong era, when Lu Hongzheng managed the salt monopoly, he recommended Yu as commissioner of the monopoly salt at the two pools of Anyi.

sentences.zh: 先是，法疏闊，吏輕觸禁，輿為立約數十條，莫不以為宜。

translations.literal: Earlier the laws had been loose and clerks lightly violated prohibitions; Yu established several dozen articles of agreement, and all held them fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the laws had been loose and clerks lightly violated prohibitions; Yu established several dozen articles of agreement, and all held them fitting.

sentences.zh: 以勞再遷戶部郎中。

translations.literal: For his labor he was twice promoted to Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was twice promoted to director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 圖，咸通末擢進士，禮部侍郎王凝特所獎待，俄而凝坐法貶商州，圖感知己，往從之。

translations.literal: Tu, at the end of Xiantong, passed the jinshi; Vice Director of Rites Wang Ning especially prized and treated him; soon Ning was demoted to Shangzhou for a legal offense and Tu, moved by gratitude to his patron, went to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Tu passed the jinshi at the end of Xiantong; Vice Director of Rites Wang Ning especially prized him; soon Ning was demoted to Shangzhou for a legal offense and Tu, moved by gratitude, went to follow him.

sentences.zh: 凝起拜宣歙觀察使，乃辟置幕府。

translations.literal: When Ning was raised and appointed Observation Commissioner of Xuan and She, he recruited Tu to his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Ning was raised and appointed observation commissioner of Xuan and She, he recruited Tu to his staff.

sentences.zh: 召為殿中侍御史，不忍去凝府，臺劾，左遷光祿寺主簿，分司東都。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Attending Censor but could not bear to leave Ning's headquarters; the Censorate impeached him and he was demoted to Master of Records in the Court of Imperial Entertainments, serving at the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as attending censor but could not bear to leave Ning's headquarters; the censorate impeached him and he was demoted to master of records in the Court of Imperial Entertainments, serving at the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 盧攜以故宰相居洛，嘉圖節，常與遊。

translations.literal: Lu Xie, a former chief minister living in Luoyang, admired Tu's integrity and often went about with him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xie, a former chief minister living in Luoyang, admired Tu's integrity and often kept his company.

sentences.zh: 攜還朝，過陜虢，屬於觀察使盧渥曰：「司空御史，高士也。

translations.literal: When Xie returned to court, passing through Shan and Guo, he said to Observation Commissioner Lu Wo: "Censor Sikong is a lofty gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: When Xie returned to court, passing through Shan and Guo, he said to observation commissioner Lu Wo: "Censor Sikong is a lofty gentleman."

sentences.zh: 」渥即表為僚佐。

translations.literal: Wo thereupon memorialized him as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Wo thereupon recommended him as staff officer.

sentences.zh: 會攜復執政，召拜禮部員外郎，尋遷郎中。

translations.literal: When Xie again held power he summoned Tu as Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, soon promoting him to Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie again held power he summoned Tu as vice director of the Ministry of Rites, soon promoting him to director.

sentences.zh: 黃巢陷長安，將奔，不得前。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao took Chang'an, Tu wished to flee but could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao took Chang'an, Tu wished to flee but could not get through.

sentences.zh: 圖弟有奴段章者，陷賊，執圖手曰：「我所主張將軍喜下士，可往見之，無虛死溝中。

translations.literal: Tu's younger brother had a slave named Duan Zhang who had fallen to the rebels; he seized Tu's hand and said: "The master I serve, General, delights in receiving gentlemen—go see him; do not die uselessly in a ditch."
translations.idiomatic: Tu's younger brother had a slave named Duan Zhang who had fallen to the rebels; he seized Tu's hand and said: "The master I serve delights in receiving gentlemen—go see him; do not die uselessly in a ditch."

sentences.zh: 」圖不肯往，章泣下。

translations.literal: Tu would not go; Zhang wept.
translations.idiomatic: Tu would not go; Zhang wept.

sentences.zh: 遂奔咸陽，間關至河中。

translations.literal: He then fled to Xianyang and, by perilous paths, reached Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: He then fled to Xianyang and, by perilous paths, reached Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 僖宗次鳳翔，即行在拜知制誥，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong halted at Fengxiang, the temporary capital, and immediately appointed Tu Drafting Secretary and promoted him to Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong halted at Fengxiang as temporary capital and immediately appointed Tu drafting secretary, then promoted him to attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後狩寶雞，不獲從，又還河中。

translations.literal: Later when the emperor hunted at Baoji, Tu could not follow and returned again to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Later when the emperor hunted at Baoji, Tu could not follow and returned to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 龍紀初，復拜舊官，以疾解。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longji he was again appointed to his former office but resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Longji he was again appointed to his former office but resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 景福中，拜諫議大夫，不赴。

translations.literal: In the Jingfu era he was appointed Remonstrator but did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingfu era he was appointed remonstrator but did not go.

sentences.zh: 後再以戶部侍郎召，身謝闕下，數日即引去。

translations.literal: Later he was again summoned as Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue; he came in person to decline at the palace gate and within days withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was again summoned as vice director of the Ministry of Revenue; he came in person to decline at the palace gate and within days withdrew.

sentences.zh: 昭宗在華，召拜兵部侍郎，以足疾固自乞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong was at Hua he summoned Tu as Vice Director of the Ministry of War; on grounds of foot ailment he firmly begged off.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong was at Hua he summoned Tu as vice director of the Ministry of War; on grounds of foot ailment he firmly begged off.

sentences.zh: 會遷洛陽，柳璨希賊臣意，誅天下才望，助喪王室，詔圖入朝，圖陽墮笏，趣意野耄。

translations.literal: When the court moved to Luoyang, Liu Can, hoping to please the wicked ministers, slaughtered the empire's talent and renown to aid the ruined royal house; an edict summoned Tu to court; Tu pretended to drop his tablet and affected the manner of a rustic old man.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved to Luoyang, Liu Can, hoping to please the wicked ministers, slaughtered the empire's talent to aid the ruined royal house; an edict summoned Tu to court; Tu pretended to drop his tablet and affected the manner of a rustic old man.

sentences.zh: 璨知無意於世，乃聽還。

translations.literal: Can knew he had no intent toward the world and let him return.
translations.idiomatic: Can knew he had no intent toward the world and let him return.

sentences.zh: 圖本居中條山王官谷，有先人田，遂隱不出。

translations.literal: Tu had long dwelt at Wangguan Valley on Mount Zhongtiao, with ancestral fields, and so hid himself and did not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Tu had long dwelt at Wangguan Valley on Mount Zhongtiao, with ancestral fields, and so hid himself and did not emerge.

sentences.zh: 作亭觀素室，悉圖唐興節士文人，名亭曰休休，作文以見誌曰：「休，美也，既休而美具。

translations.literal: He built a plain pavilion and lodge, painting all the Tang's men of integrity and literary men; he named the pavilion Xiuxiu and wrote a text to show his aim: "Xiu means beautiful; once xiu, beauty is complete."
translations.idiomatic: He built a plain pavilion and lodge, painting all the Tang's men of integrity and literary men; he named the pavilion Xiuxiu and wrote a text to show his aim: "Xiu means beautiful; once at rest, beauty is complete."

sentences.zh: 故量才，一宜休；

translations.literal: Therefore to measure talent—first reason to rest;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore to measure talent—first reason to rest;

sentences.zh: 揣分，二宜休；

translations.literal: to gauge one's portion—second reason to rest;
translations.idiomatic: to gauge one's portion—second reason to rest;

sentences.zh: 耄而聵，三宜休；

translations.literal: old and deaf—third reason to rest;
translations.idiomatic: old and deaf—third reason to rest;

sentences.zh: 又少也惰，長也率，老也迂，三者非濟時用，則又宜休。

translations.literal: and again, in youth I was lazy, in maturity I was careless, in age I am obstinate—these three are not useful in aiding the age, so again one should rest.
translations.idiomatic: and again, in youth I was lazy, in maturity I was careless, in age I am obstinate—these three are not useful in aiding the age, so again one should rest.

sentences.zh: 」因自目為耐辱居士。

translations.literal: He therefore styled himself the Recluse Who Endures Insult.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore styled himself the Recluse Who Endures Insult.

sentences.zh: 其言詭激不常，以免當時禍災雲。

translations.literal: His words were eccentric and sharp, not constant, to escape the calamities of the time, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: His words were eccentric and sharp, not constant, to escape the calamities of the time, it is said.

sentences.zh: 豫為冢棺，遇勝日，引客坐壙中賦詩，酌酒裴回。

translations.literal: He prepared his tomb and coffin in advance; on fine days he would lead guests to sit in the burial pit, compose poetry, and pour wine while pacing about.
translations.idiomatic: He prepared his tomb and coffin in advance; on fine days he would lead guests to sit in the burial pit, compose poetry, and pour wine while pacing about.

sentences.zh: 客或難之，圖曰：「君何不廣邪？

translations.literal: When guests objected, Tu said: "Why not broaden your view?"
translations.idiomatic: When guests objected, Tu said: "Why not broaden your view?"

sentences.zh: 生死一致，吾寧暫遊此中哉！

translations.literal: Life and death are one; would I not rather wander awhile in this place!"
translations.idiomatic: Life and death are one; would I not rather wander awhile in this place!"

sentences.zh: 」每歲時，祠禱鼓舞，圖與閭里耆老相樂。

translations.literal: Each year at the seasons he offered prayers with drum and dance; Tu rejoiced together with the elders of the village.
translations.idiomatic: Each year at the seasons he offered prayers with drum and dance; Tu rejoiced together with the elders of the village.

sentences.zh: 王重榮父子雅重之，數饋遺，弗受。

translations.literal: Wang Chongrong, father and son, esteemed him highly and often sent gifts, which he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chongrong, father and son, esteemed him highly and often sent gifts, which he would not accept.

sentences.zh: 嘗為作碑，贈絹數千，圖置虞鄉市，人得取之，一日盡。

translations.literal: Once when he wrote a stele for them they gave him several thousand bolts of silk; Tu placed them in the market at Yuxiang for anyone to take, and in one day they were gone.
translations.idiomatic: Once when he wrote a stele for them they gave him several thousand bolts of silk; Tu placed them in the market at Yuxiang for anyone to take, and in one day they were gone.

sentences.zh: 時寇盜所過殘暴，獨不入王官谷，士人依以避難。

translations.literal: When bandits passed through they were brutal everywhere, yet they did not enter Wangguan Valley; scholars relied on it to escape harm.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits passed through they were brutal everywhere, yet they did not enter Wangguan Valley; scholars relied on it to escape harm.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠已篡，召為禮部尚書，不起。

translations.literal: After Zhu Quanzhong had usurped power he summoned Tu as Director of the Ministry of Rites, but Tu would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu Quanzhong had usurped power he summoned Tu as director of the Ministry of Rites, but Tu would not rise.

sentences.zh: 哀帝弒，圖聞，不食而卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ai was murdered, Tu heard of it, stopped eating, and died at seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ai was murdered, Tu heard of it, stopped eating, and died at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 圖無子，以甥為嗣，嘗為御史所劾，昭宗不責也。

translations.literal: Tu had no sons and made a nephew his heir; once he was impeached by a censor but Emperor Zhaozong did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Tu had no sons and made a nephew his heir; once he was impeached by a censor but Emperor Zhaozong did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：節誼為天下大閑，士不可不勉。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Integrity and righteousness are the great standard of the empire; scholars cannot but strive for them.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Integrity and righteousness are the great standard of the empire; scholars cannot but strive for them.

sentences.zh: 觀臯、濟不汙賊，據忠自完，而亂臣為沮計。

translations.literal: Consider how Gao and Ji were not defiled by rebels, holding to loyalty to preserve themselves, while rebellious ministers devised schemes to thwart them.
translations.idiomatic: Consider how Gao and Ji were not defiled by rebels, holding to loyalty to preserve themselves, while rebellious ministers devised schemes to thwart them.

sentences.zh: 天下士知大分所在，故傾朝復支。

translations.literal: Scholars throughout the empire knew where the greater duty lay, and so the court was restored and supported.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars throughout the empire knew where the greater duty lay, and so the court was restored and supported.

sentences.zh: 不有君子，果能國乎？

translations.literal: Without gentlemen, can the state indeed stand?
translations.idiomatic: Without gentlemen, can the state indeed stand?

sentences.zh: 德秀以德，城以鯁峭，圖知命，其志凜凜與秋霜爭嚴，真丈夫哉！

translations.literal: Dexiu by virtue, Cheng by blunt integrity, Tu by knowing fate—their aims contended with autumn frost in severity; true husbands indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Dexiu by virtue, Cheng by blunt integrity, Tu by knowing fate—their aims contended with autumn frost in severity; true men indeed!
